title: Implications of recent clinical trials for the National Cholesterol Education Program Adult Treatment Panel III guidelines
authors: Grundy SM, Cleeman JI, Merz CN, Brewer HB Jr, Clark LT, Hunninghake DB, et al.
funder: not stated; approved by the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute, the American Heart Association and the American College of Cardiology Foundation
authorConflicts: Financial disclosure published by the NHLBI: of nine working group members, eight reported relationships with manufacturers of lipid-lowering drugs. Grundy: honoraria from Merck, Pfizer, Sankyo, Bayer, Merck/Schering-Plough, Kos, Abbott, Bristol-Myers Squibb and AstraZeneca and research grants from Merck, Abbott and GlaxoSmithKline. Bairey Merz: lecture honoraria from Pfizer, Merck and Kos, consultancy for Pfizer, Bayer and EHC (Merck), research grant from Merck, stock in several companies. result: Based on five statin trials published after 2001 (including HPS and PROVE IT), the update kept an LDL cholesterol goal below 100 mg/dL for high-risk people but made a goal below 70 mg/dL a therapeutic option for very high risk, including people with baseline LDL below 100 mg/dL; for moderately high-risk people (2 or more risk factors, 10-year risk 10 to 20%) the goal stayed below 130 mg/dL with below 100 mg/dL as an option; drug therapy should lower LDL cholesterol by at least 30 to 40%. The authors state that HPS and PROVE IT cannot be taken as the final word on lowering LDL well below 100 mg/dL.
